objective: Standard statement: (1) Hall: a cubic bipartite graph that is cyclically 4-edge-connected is a brace; (2) weaving lemma: if a connected cubic bipartite source is drawn with its vertices in distinct faces of a cyclically 4-edge-connected planar cubic bipartite frame, edges in general position, then the planarized host with a ladder site at every crossing is cyclically 4-edge-connected; (3) cube junction lemma: gluing two cubes onto a 4-cycle of a cyclically 4-edge-connected cubic graph (square edges deleted) keeps it cyclically 4-edge-connected; (4) Theorem: counting proper 2-colourings of 3-regular 3-uniform hypergraphs whose incidence graphs are Pfaffian braces is #P-hard (Turing), with prism frames and cube pages; the woven count is #col(source) #col(frame); (5) with Valiant's planar algorithm and the Heawood graph: planar plain braces count in polynomial time, the knot's atom trivially, and the class in general is #P-hard. Checks: woven instances of a non-brace source are cyclically 4-edge-connected hosts and certified Pfaffian; small woven instances pass the direct brace test; single-site interpolation inside a woven instance recovers the count with that site uncrossed; ladder sites and cube junctions verified by exhaustive cut checks on small cases; control: the source drawn without a frame keeps its 2-edge cut. Nearest known result: Fan-Cai 2020 (hardness on general graphs); none for braces found.
status: Proved: counting 2-colourings of 3-regular 3-uniform hypergraphs with Pfaffian brace incidence graphs is #P-hard (Turing): a hard source woven into a prism frame with ladder sites of plain cube junctions; bond, weaving and cube junction lemmas give cyclic 4-edge-connectivity, Hall gives a brace. Among plain Pfaffian braces planarity and the knot's atom are the polynomial cases found; the class is hard.
title: Counting on plain Pfaffian braces is #P-hard
